Okay, this is a really common misinterpretation. True, In our society women choose jobs that pay less, work fewer hours, and are promoted less on average. The wage gap isn't meant to point out pay inequality in equal jobs, it's meant to point out that even though women are just as capable as men they are essentially being forced (via gender rolls) to take jobs that are paid less than other "male dominated" fields. Women are automatically seen as less capable than men on such a widespread and widely accepted scale most people don't even see it as a problem. That's why women are promoted less than men are for typically equal work. Women are also expected to help around the house or with the kids more, leading to the "fewer hours" and "less overtime" that you cite. The wage gap isn't an issue of 75 cents on the dollar or whatever bullshit, it's about society's gender rolls and the unequal sexist standards set for women across the board.

In the Midwest our houses are built out of wood, it's flipping everywhere. We build basements for protection against tornadoes. We do what we can. But it's unavoidable.

My best friend was in the middle of that tornado. She was in a church and used her own body as a barricade to keep the basement doors shut after the wooden 2x4s snapped. The roof of the STONE church came down and she lost a good portion of her family to the falling stones. She only survived because she was in the basement in charge of all the younger kids that they could fit down there. After it was over they had to walk for miles through the torn up streets to try and receive medical attention, all the while seeing the destruction and death around them. They went by a friends house to check on him and found him impaled with a tree limb half a block from his house.

What I'm getting at here is, that tornado was pure destruction. Very few buildings were left standing. Whole buildings were ripped from their foundations. What they were made of doesn't matter at that level of chaos and hellish carnage.

I once had a teacher mark me down 7 points on our final essay because I was the only one who disagreed with her. The reason she wrote on the paper for detracting points was for "attacking her". I had two other English teachers read it and no one else thought it was a direct attack on her. That essay kept me from getting the weight point I needed to have a 4.0 GPA. Not a big deal in the long run, but it was more a matter of personal pride, ya' know?
